paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : Wait-k Policy
model_annotation: The figure illustrates the relationship between BLEU score and Average Lagging (AL) for three different consistency-based policies in simultaneous machine translation, as evaluated under a wait-k policy. The vertical axis (BLEU) ranges from 20 to 30, marked at intervals of 2, and uses a linear scale; the horizontal axis (Average Lagging, AL) ranges from 0 to 8, also marked at intervals of 2, and is linear. Three distinct lines represent different methods: “Consistency-CE” (blue dashed line with circle markers), “Consistency-Bi + sampling” (orange dash-dotted line with triangle markers), and “Consistency-Bi + beam” (green dotted line with square markers). All three methods show an increasing trend in BLEU score as AL increases. At AL=0, “Consistency-CE” starts at approximately BLEU 19, while “Consistency-Bi + sampling” begins around BLEU 24.2 and “Consistency-Bi + beam” at about BLEU 23.2. By AL=8, “Consistency-CE” reaches approximately BLEU 28.8, “Consistency-Bi + sampling” reaches about 29.4, and “Consistency-Bi + beam” reaches roughly 29.2. The legend is positioned in the lower-left corner, clearly associating each line style and marker with its corresponding method. The chart includes horizontal dashed gridlines to aid in reading BLEU values. Overall, “Consistency-Bi + sampling” consistently achieves the highest BLEU scores across most AL values, followed closely by “Consistency-Bi + beam,” while “Consistency-CE” lags behind but still improves significantly with higher AL.
